notes:
Snapshot: mid-market/enterprise headless commerce platform with 35M active SKUs (catalog + variants). Primary pain: search quality and cost volatility during seasonal peaks. Current infra: ES for text search + in-house sparse features; experimenting with vector-based recall + ML reranker for top-K reordering.

Business goals / constraints:
- Target p95 search latency <= 120ms for typical queries; 95th during spikes allowed to 250ms.
- Cost-per-query target (avg) <= $0.003 (embeddings + rerank amortized).
- Need autoscale plan to handle 6-10x traffic spikes during promotions (Black Friday, Prime week).
- Strong requirement for VPC private deployment + SOC2 compliance and KMS integration for keys. EU customers require data residency (store embeddings in eu-west only).

Technical notes from discovery call (2025-02-05, Maya/Luis):
- "We see a 7x increase in read QPS during promos; current infra can't keep cost predictable." — Head of Search product.
- POC scope agreed: ingest 50M product embeddings (avg 1536-dim), implement hybrid recall (keyword+ANN), run learned reranker on top-10 using customer-provided pairwise labels.
- Expected QPS baseline: 300 qps global, spike to 2100 qps peak (short bursts).
- Throughput target: sustained 25 qps per GPU, need fleet sizing guidance and burst capacity strategy.

Evaluation criteria (Citrine):
- Recall@50 and MRR improvement vs current ES baseline (>15% improvement target).
- Latency (recall + rerank) p95 under 250ms, avg <120ms.
- Clear unit economics: cost/query including embedding storage and reranker compute. Prefer provider that can model seasonal commit vs pay-as-you-go.
- Ops: shop for realtime monitoring, traceability, token-level cost breakdowns. Need audit logs for every index update and inference.

POC plan / milestones:
- Week 0: Access + sample data ingest (10M rows), security review (SAML + KMS).
- Week 1: Index build + vector store baseline (measure ingest time, storage footprint).
- Week 2: End-to-end queries with candidate recall + rerank; measure latency and accuracy.
- Week 3: Load test for 6x traffic spike; validate autoscale and fallback policies; cost modeling run.

Notes / Objections recorded:
- Engineering: migration complexity from legacy product IDs and variant mapping; need helpers for ID mapping and upserts.
- Procurement: prefers committed capacity pricing for peak windows (wants a 'burst pool' pricing option).
- Security: will run a separate security questionnaire; wants Redwood to sign DPA with EU residency addendum.

Internal AE playbook items:
- Send Redwood Dedicated sizing doc + sample pricing scenarios by 2025-02-21.
- Coordinate SE deep-dive with Luis week of 2025-02-24 to discuss quantization options for embeddings and batching knobs.
- Attach Fireflies call and initial ingest checklist to Drive (link above).

Quick quotes from contact:
- "If we can halve our cost-per-query for peak events while improving MRR, it's a no-brainer to move."
- "We need clear SLAs for Black Friday window; can't gamble on spot capacity."
